newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Fujimori does not rule out third term.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Fujimori does not rule out third term.

text.p: Peru's President Alberto Fujimori, whose popularity has soared since he sent in troops to end a four-month hostage crisis in Lima last month, said on Friday he would not rule out running for a third term as president.
"If a small window of opportunity opens up, it could happen," he said in an interview broadcast by television channel CBS-Telenoticias.
Fujimori said though that he was not concentrating on the issue right now. The next presidential elections are due in 2000.
Fujimori, the son of Japanese immigrants, came to power in 1990 and won reelection in 1995 after a 1992 "self-coup" in which he dissolved parliament.

Opponents of another Fujimori term have raised legal objections to his running again. Peruvian law forbids a president who has been elected for two consecutive terms from seeking the office again in the next election.

In August, though, Congress voted in favour of a legal interpretation that meant his first term would not be counted if he wished to stand again in 2000. That interpretation was based on the fact that after his "self-coup", a reformulated Congress passed a new Constitution.

Fujimori said the April 22 hostage rescue mission at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima, in which all 14 Marxist rebels died along with one hostage and two soldiers, was an operation planned "millimeter by millimetre" which nevertheless almost went wrong in various ways.
"I took the decision because I was 100 percent sure that it would turn out all right," Fujimori said. "I was sure because it was rehearsed."
He said though that the crack troops who stormed the residence took twice as long as planned to carry out the operation, which caused him some "concern".

One hostage unexpectedly hid in a closet while two rebels of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement hid upstairs at the residence and started throwing hand grenades, he said. The assault troops quickly killed them.
The operation freed the remaining 71 hostages alive.
